estimate_trade.description: Work out what buying or selling a given amount would cost at the prices actually on the order book - the average price you would get, and how far that is from the headline price. A small trade fills at the top of the book; a large one eats into the levels behind it, and that difference is worth knowing before you commit. Say the amount in coin ('buy 2 ETH') or in money ('spend 5,000 USD'). This is an estimate from the book at one instant and excludes fees; it does not place anything. No API key required.

get_order_book.description: See what is waiting to be bought and sold on a market, and at what prices. Each side comes back with a running total, so 'how much could I sell before the price drops below X' is a value to read rather than a sum to do. Coinbase's own book runs to about 21,000 price levels; this brings back the ones nearest the current price, which is where trading actually happens. No API key required.

get_price_history.description: Get a market's price over time as candles - the open, high, low, close and volume of each minute, hour, six hours or day - for a chart, a moving average, or comparing this week against last. Coinbase caps a single request at 300 candles; a longer window is fetched in pages here, so ask for the window you want. Candles come back oldest first with named fields, along with the high, the low and the change across the whole window. No API key required.

get_recent_trades.description: Get the trades that have just gone through on a market - each one's price, size, time and which way it went - with the buying and the selling totalled up so you can see which side is pushing. Coinbase reports a trade from the side of the order that was already resting on the book, so its 'buy' means somebody sold; each trade here is reported from the side that crossed the spread instead, which is the one people mean. No API key required.

description: Read the live market data of Coinbase Exchange, the institutional venue behind Coinbase. Get what any of its 500-plus markets is trading at, how it has moved over the last 24 hours, and its price history as candles going back years. Look into the order book, follow the trades as they print, and work out what buying or selling a given amount would actually cost once it eats through the book. Every price comes back as a number rather than text, so a step can compare it straight away. No account or API key required - and every action reads, so nothing here can reach an account or move money.
